research_questions.statement: What are the properties and limitations of neighborhood aggregation schemes for graph representation learning?

provenance.text_excerpt: we observe that the influence distributions of networks with residual connections approximately correspond to lazy random walks: each step has a higher probability of staying at the current node. Local information is retained with similar probabilities for all nodes in each iteration; this cannot adapt to diverse needs of specific upper-layer nodes.

claims.statement: Residual connections in GCNs lead to influence distributions similar to lazy random walks, retaining local information.

provenance.text_excerpt: The following results show that the influence distributions of common aggregation schemes are closely connected to random walk distributions.

claims.statement: The influence distribution of common neighborhood aggregation schemes is closely connected to random walk distributions.

datasets.description: Used for illustration of random walk expansion in different subgraph structures.
datasets.name: GooglePlus social network

experiments_or_tasks: Analyze the effect of residual connections on influence distributions.
Analyze the effective range (influence distribution) of nodes in neighborhood aggregation schemes.
Connect influence distributions to random walk distributions on graphs.
Visualize influence distributions of trained GCNs and compare with random walk distributions.

methods.name: Influence Distribution Computation
methods.protocol_description: Define influence distribution Ix(y) as the sum over paths from x to y of the product of normalized derivatives along the path. Under a randomization assumption on ReLU activations, show equivalence to random walk distributions.

study_units.name: Influence Distribution Analysis

provenance.text_excerpt: we observe that the influence distributions of networks with residual connections approximately correspond to lazy random walks: each step has a higher probability of staying at the current node.

results.value_raw_text: Influence distributions of GCNs with residual connections approximately correspond to lazy random walks.

provenance.text_excerpt: We visualize the heat maps of the influence distributions for a node (labeled square) for trained GCNs, and compare with the random walk distributions starting at the same node. Figure 2 shows example results.

results.value_raw_text: Heat maps of influence distributions for trained GCNs closely match random walk distributions.

provenance.text_excerpt: Given a k-layer GCN with averaging as in Equation (3), assume that all paths in the computation graph of the model are activated with the same probability of success ρ. Then the influence distribution Ix for any node x ∈V is equivalent, in expectation, to the k-step random walk distribution on eG starting at node x.

results.value_raw_text: The influence distribution of a k-layer GCN with averaging is equivalent, in expectation, to the k-step random walk distribution on the augmented graph.

provenance.text_excerpt: Models that impose a fixed random walk distribution inherit these discrepancies in the speed of expansion and influence neighborhoods, which may not lead to the best representations for all nodes.

claims.statement: Fixed neighborhood aggregation schemes impose a structure-dependent influence radius that may not be optimal for all nodes.

experiments_or_tasks: Discuss the implications of fixed random walk distributions on graphs with varying subgraph structures.
Illustrate fast collapse on expanders and slow convergence on tree-like parts.
study_units.name: Limitations of Fixed Aggregation Schemes

provenance.text_excerpt: Random walks starting inside an expander converge rapidly in O(log |V |) steps to an almost-uniform distribution (Hoory et al., 2006).

results.value_raw_text: Random walks on expanders converge in O(log |V|) steps to almost-uniform distribution.

research_questions.statement: Can an adaptive architecture that learns to select neighborhood ranges per node improve graph representation learning?

provenance.text_excerpt: Figure 5 illustrates how a 6-layer JK-Net with max-pooling aggregation learns to adapt to different subgraph structures on a citation network.

claims.statement: JK-Nets adaptively learn different neighborhood ranges for nodes in different subgraph structures.

datasets.description: Used for visualization of JK-Net adaptivity.
datasets.name: Citation network (unspecified)

experiments_or_tasks: Visualize how a 6-layer JK-Net with max-pooling adapts influence on a citation network.
study_units.name: JK-Net Adaptivity Visualization

provenance.text_excerpt: Within a tree-like structure, the influence stays in the 'small community' the node belongs to. ... For a node affiliated to a 'hub', ... JK-Net learns to put most influence on the node itself and otherwise spreads out the influence. ... For hubs, JK-Net spreads out the influence across the neighboring nodes in a reasonable range.

results.value_raw_text: JK-Net learns to focus influence on small community for tree-like nodes, on self for hub-affiliated nodes, and spreads influence for hubs.

provenance.text_excerpt: Contrasting this result with the influence distributions of other aggregation mechanisms, we see that JK-networks indeed differ in their node-wise adaptivity of neighborhood ranges.

claims.statement: JK-Nets enable node-wise adaptivity of neighborhood ranges, unlike fixed aggregation schemes.

experiments_or_tasks: Analyze adaptivity of JK-Nets via influence distributions.
Propose JK-Nets with layer aggregation mechanisms: concatenation, max-pooling, LSTM-attention.

methods.name: JK-Net with Concatenation
methods.protocol_description: Concatenate representations from all layers and apply a linear transformation. Weights are shared across nodes, not node-adaptive.

methods.name: JK-Net with Max-pooling
methods.protocol_description: Element-wise max over layer representations. Adaptive per node, no additional parameters.

methods.name: JK-Net with LSTM-attention
methods.protocol_description: Input layer representations into a bi-directional LSTM, compute attention scores via linear mapping and softmax, and take weighted sum. Node-adaptive.

study_units.name: Jumping Knowledge Networks (JK-Nets) Design

provenance.text_excerpt: The influence score I(x, y) for any x, y ∈V under a k-layer JK-Net with layer-wise max-pooling is equivalent in expectation to a mixture of 0, .., k-step random walk distributions on eG at y starting at x, the coefficients of which depend on the values of the layer features h(l)x.

results.value_raw_text: Under JK-Net with max-pooling, the influence score is equivalent in expectation to a mixture of 0 to k-step random walk distributions, with coefficients depending on layer features.

research_questions.statement: How do JK-Nets perform compared to state-of-the-art models on node classification benchmarks?

provenance.text_excerpt: With MaxPool as node aggregator and Concat as layer aggregator, JK-Net achieves the best Micro-F1 score among GarphSAGE and JK-Net variants. Note that the original GraphSAGE already performs fairly well with a Micro-F1 of 0.95. JK-Net reduces the error by 30%.

claims.statement: JK-Net with MaxPool node aggregator and Concat layer aggregator achieves best Micro-F1 of 0.965 on Reddit, reducing error by 30% over GraphSAGE.
